description: SAMPLE / TABLESAMPLE row sampling, asserted through the DETERMINISTIC cases only: 100 percent keeps all rows, 0 percent keeps none, a fixed n ROWS keeps exactly n and is capped at the table size, TABLESAMPLE is an accepted synonym of SAMPLE, and the BERNOULLI / ROW / SYSTEM methods all parse and run. A REPEATABLE seed makes FRACTIONAL sampling reproducible, and SEED is an accepted synonym for REPEATABLE. Converted 1:1 from query/SampleClauseTest (now retired); the Java compared two Java HashSets of ids to show the seed reproduces its rows, which becomes a two-way EXCEPT between the two identically-seeded queries - the same claim, made in SQL.

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s SAMPLE (3 ROWS)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s SAMPLE (100 ROWS)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s TABLESAMPLE (4 ROWS)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s SAMPLE BERNOULLI (100)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s SAMPLE ROW (100)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s SAMPLE SYSTEM (100)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ((SELECT id FROM s SAMPLE (50) REPEATABLE (42)) EXCEPT (SELECT id FROM s SAMPLE (50) REPEATABLE (42)))
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ((SELECT id FROM s SAMPLE (50) REPEATABLE (42)) EXCEPT (SELECT id FROM s SAMPLE (50) REPEATABLE (42))) x
SELECT COUNT(*) <= 10 FROM s SAMPLE (50) SEED (42)
